NO CABIN YET
Week 8 · Writing Organized Paragraphs

Carry-On Only

In the DET Writing Sample you have only 5 minutes, so you can't take a big suitcase. You need one small, well-packed bag: a tag on the outside (the topic sentence), the right things inside (supporting ideas with details and examples), and a zip to close it (the concluding sentence). This week every sentence has a colour, so you can see how a paragraph is packed. Every activity has a Fly again button. There's no grade, and finishing the steps counts as attending this week.

~25 min total Choose your level No sound needed One 5-minute paragraph
?Not sure what to do? Tap ? How it works at the top of any stop. You will see pictures and easy steps.
TagTopic sentence: a topic + a controlling idea
PackSupporting ideas, each with a detail or example
ZipA concluding sentence that closes the paragraph
STOP 01~1 min

Choose Your Cabin

Pick the level that feels right today. Your choice changes the paragraphs you read and how much you write. Every cabin counts the same for attendance, and you can switch any time.

STOP 02~3 min

Pre-flight Briefing

DET QUESTION · WRITING SAMPLE

The Writing Sample gives you one question, 30 seconds to plan and 5 minutes to write. It is scored on content, coherence (organization), grammar and vocabulary, and universities read your answer. One clear paragraph is enough. A well-organized paragraph has four kinds of sentence. Look at the colours:

Topic sentenceNames the topic and gives a controlling idea about it.
Supporting ideaA reason or point that explains the topic sentence.
Detail or exampleSomething specific about the supporting idea just before it.
Concluding sentenceCloses the paragraph.

Now match each kind of sentence to its job: tap a name, then tap its job.

STOP 03~5 min

Label the Bag

PARAGRAPH SKILL · TOPIC SENTENCE

The topic sentence is the tag on your bag. It tells the reader what is inside before they open it.

A strong tag = topic + controlling idea

The topic is what the paragraph is about. The controlling idea is what you want to say about the topic. It controls every other sentence in the paragraph.

✗ WEAK TAGI live near a café.This is only a fact. The next sentence could be about anything: the coffee, the price, your house…
✓ STRONG TAGThe café near my house is a great place to study.Now the reader expects every other sentence to show why that café is a great place to study.

PART AStrong tag or weak tag?

PART BChoose the best topic sentence

Each paragraph has lost its first sentence. Choose the tag that fits everything in the bag: not too narrow, not too broad.

STOP 04~4 min

Security Check

PARAGRAPH SKILL · UNITY

At security, anything that doesn't belong comes out of the bag. In a good paragraph, every sentence supports the controlling idea in the topic sentence. In each paragraph below, one sentence must come out. Tap it. The first sentence is the tag, so it always stays.

TIPAsk each sentence: "Do you help to show the controlling idea?" If the answer is no, it comes out, even when it is true and interesting.
STOP 05~5 min

Pack in Order

PARAGRAPH SKILL · COHERENCE

A good packer puts things in the bag in order: the tag first, each supporting idea followed by its detail or example, and the zip last. These sentences are mixed up. Tap them in the right order to pack the bag, then tap Check.

TIPLook for clue words: connectors (First, For example, However) and words that point back (this, that, their, the result).
STOP 06~4 min

Zip It Up

PARAGRAPH SKILL · CONCLUDING SENTENCE

The concluding sentence closes the bag. There are four good ways to do it, and one way that leaves the bag open.

TYPEWHAT IT DOESSIGNAL PHRASES
RestateSays the topic sentence again in new wordsFor these reasons, All in all, Clearly
Sum upNames your supporting ideas in a few wordsIn short, To sum up
Result or lessonSays what changed, or what you learnedAs a result, This taught me that
Look aheadGives a plan, a hope or some adviceIn the future, I hope to, I recommend
✗ New topicStarts a new idea, so the bag stays openAlso, By the way

This paragraph has no ending. Below are five possible last sentences. Tap the type of each one.

STOP 07~8 min

Full Flight

DET PRACTICE · WRITING SAMPLE

Now pack your own bag. Just like the real Writing Sample: read the question, 30 seconds to plan, then 5 minutes to write one organized paragraph. After that, you will colour your own sentences and compare with a model.

STOP 08~2 min

Landing Card
